title: Add incident-bot snippet templates for KMS incidents (signals, links, and evidence checklist)
author: Kira Thompson
description: Problem: during the KMS failure-mode tests and recent canary brownout, on-call responders captured different sets of data (missing key IDs, breaker state, provider error codes), which slowed triage and made post-incident evidence inconsistent. This PR adds standardized incident-bot snippet templates for KMS-related incidents (timeouts/throttling/AccessDenied/Disabled keys/region outages) with: (1) a minimal data-to-capture checklist, (2) links to the canonical dashboards, (3) links to the KMS degradation runbook + escalation guidance, and (4) a short customer-impact summary template that avoids leaking sensitive key identifiers. Scope: incident-bot templates only (no production code changes). Follow-ups: we’ll wire these into the /inc start flow once the templates settle, and we’ll update the on-call playbook to reference the same snippet IDs.
commits: incident-bot: add KMS incident snippet templates + quick links
docs: add guidance on sanitizing key identifiers in external comms
chore: add snippet validation test + CI check
notable_snippet_excerpt:
Snippet: kms_degradation
Title: KMS dependency degradation (timeouts/throttling)
Checklist (copy/paste):
- Time window (UTC): <start>–<end>
- Affected environment: hosted | dedicated | private | staging
- Affected provider: aws-kms | gcp-kms | azure-key-vault | unknown
- Services/regions: <svc>/<region>
- Symptoms: elevated decrypt failures | elevated encrypt latency | breaker open | cache TTL changes
- Error codes (top 3): <e.g., ThrottlingException, Timeout, AccessDenied>
- Circuit breaker state: <closed|open|half-open> (include threshold + current rate)
- Cache: hit rate %, TTL, recent changes
- Customer impact: <tenants count>, <routes>, <estimated request failures>
Links:
- Dashboard: KMS Overview (latency/errors/breaker/cache)
- Dashboard: Tenant impact summary (admin)
- Runbook: KMS Dependency Degradation
Escalation:
- Page Security if AccessDenied/KeyDisabled suspected or key policy changes occurred
- Page Platform if config drift / key version pinning issues suspected
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Love this—matches what we struggled with in the canary. Two nits: (1) can we add a field for ‘last known good’ deployment or config change? (2) Please ensure we don’t instruct people to paste full key ARNs into Slack channels that might be shared with customers. Kira Thompson (author): Added ‘Recent changes / last known good’ line to all KMS snippets and added sanitization guidance + example showing redaction (hash last 6, or use alias only). Marcus Lin (review): Please add an explicit callout for IAM deny vs key disabled vs provider throttling, and ensure the escalation section says when to involve Security vs SRE vs Platform. Kira Thompson (author): Updated the access_denied + disabled_key snippets with ‘triage hints’ and made escalation more explicit (Security for deny/disable/policy changes; SRE for brownout/outage coordination; Platform for config drift/pinning issues). Allison Grant (review): Can we link to the alert panel directly and include metric names so responders can search quickly if the dashboard link is broken? Kira Thompson (author): Added metric names under each scenario (kms.client.latency_ms, kms.client.errors_total by code, kms.breaker.state, kms.cache.hit_ratio). Connor O'Brien (review): Ship it. This will help with standardizing the incident timeline notes. Approved.
release_notes: Adds incident-bot templates for common KMS incident scenarios, including evidence checklists, dashboard/runbook links, and sanitized customer-impact summary text.
